newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Mercury secures NZ$390 mln facility.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Mercury secures NZ$390 mln facility.

text.p: Mercury Energy on Tuesday said it had organised a NZ$390 million underwritten cash advance facility with six major banks.
This is the second facility obtained this year by the company. It announced a $US270 million ($NZ390 million) revolving credit facility in April.
Mercury Energy treasurer Gary Rohloff said the facility would be used to refinance existing credit lines and it would provide support for planned domestic capital markets activity.
Mercury has a 33 percent stake in neighbouring electricity company Power NZ.
The facility was arranged by Mercury itself with commitment from ANZ Bank, ASB Bank, Bank of New Zealand, Citibank, National Bank and Westpac.
Rohloff said a recent upgrading of Standard and Poor's credit rating of Mercury to AA minus had been an advantage in arranging the facility.
